narrative.overview:
Pick Flick is one lit picture in a dark room. The current pick's backdrop fills the viewport under a warm scrim. The title, a single mono metadata line and a short reason sit in the darker part of that scrim, and everything else stays in the dark around it. The ground is a warm off-black, the text is bone, and one marquee amber marks the things you can press. Nothing else on the screen has a color of its own. The imagery comes from TMDB and supplies all the color the room needs.

The world is dark only (`color-scheme: dark`, no light tokens). Surfaces are flat. A 14% bone hairline is what separates things. The one shadow in the system belongs to the large hero poster, so the picture looks lifted off the wall. Density is low. A screen produces one pick or helps you act on one, and secondary rails (Continue watching, Trending) sit below it at a smaller scale.

Motion is a single gesture, the **reel swap**. When a new pick arrives, its backdrop, poster and text come in from a 6px blur and an 8px drop. The animation runs 480ms on an exponential ease-out (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`), and the text block follows 120ms behind the image. When `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set, the swap is turned off entirely. Controls get only a 150ms color transition and a 1px press-down.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-black room, bone text, one amber accent for pressable things.
Full-bleed backdrop under a warm scrim that is darker where the text sits.
Bricolage Grotesque display at weight 600, -0.02em tracking. Geist for UI. Geist Mono for metadata.
Hairlines instead of fills or shadows. One poster shadow.
8px corners on controls and posters, 6px on small inputs, full radius on chips and icon toggles.
One entrance animation (the reel swap), switched off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Marquee Rule
rules.body: Amber goes only on things you can press, and on the focus and selection states of those things. Headings, progress, metadata and decoration never use it. Selected segments in a segmented control use a 10% bone wash, not amber.

rules.name: The One Room Rule
rules.body: The app has one theme, and it is dark. Do not add a light variant or a second accent hue. Color for a scene comes from the TMDB imagery, never from the chrome.

rules.name: The One Marquee Rule
rules.body: Each viewport gets at most one display-scale title: the pick, or the hero line. Every other heading steps down to headline or smaller.

rules.name: The Mono Meta Rule
rules.body: Factual metadata (years, ratings, languages, counts, page numbers) is set in Geist Mono with tabular numerals, in dim bone, on one line separated by " · ". Do not put metadata in pills or badges.

rules.name: The Scrim Rule
rules.body: A full-bleed backdrop always sits under the `.scrim` layer. On desktop the scrim runs horizontally, from 92% booth-black on the left to 35% on the right, with a vertical fade to 98% at the bottom. Under 1024px it runs vertically, from 55% to 98%. Text never sits directly on a raw backdrop.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Elements are separated by a 1px border at 14% bone. Do not add background fills to make a container read as a card.

rules.name: The Lit Poster Rule
rules.body: Only the poster of the current or featured pick casts a shadow. If a second thing on the screen has a shadow, one of them is wrong.

dos: Do keep amber for pressable things and their focus or selection states (The Marquee Rule).
Do put every full-bleed image under the `.scrim` utility, which turns vertical below 1024px.
Do set titles in Bricolage Grotesque at weight 600 with -0.02em tracking, and metadata in Geist Mono with tabular numerals.
Do separate things with the 14% bone hairline, and save `shadow-poster` for the one featured poster.
Do use 8px corners on controls and posters, 6px on small inputs and segments, and full radius on chips and icon toggles.
Do bring new picks in with `.reel-swap` / `.reel-swap-late`, and keep the reduced-motion override.
Do draw icons as 16px line glyphs at 1.5 stroke.
donts: Don't use amber on headings, progress, selected segments or decorative fills.
Don't add a light theme or a second accent hue.
Don't use glassmorphism (backdrop blur), decorative glows, or gradient text. The world's only gradients are the scrim and the nav fade.
Don't put shadows on tiles, panels, buttons or menus.
Don't wrap metadata in pills or badges. It belongs on the mono meta line.
Don't put more than one display-scale title in a viewport.
